answer: Price new identities on a surge curve: each fresh agent must burn a registration fee that doubles whenever signups in the past day exceed the usual rate, then decays back slowly. Honest newcomers who arrive alone pay little and get a refund after a year of clean work, a safe harbor that makes the network a haven for real agents. An attacker spinning up a thousand sybils at once climbs the curve like a steep knoll, so the last accounts cost thousands of times the first.
